title: Sun Pharma Profit Falls 36 Percent on Organon Charge as Revenue Beats
excerpt: A Rs 1,269 crore one-time charge dragged Q2 profit to Rs 1,989 crore, while revenue rose 11.9 percent, India sales jumped 17.3 percent and shares gained about 4 percent.
body:
• Sun Pharma's Q2 FY27 net profit fell 36.2 percent to Rs 1,989 crore after a Rs 1,269 crore exceptional charge linked mainly to the Organon deal.
  • Revenue rose 11.9 percent to Rs 16,199 crore, beating the Rs 15,806 crore estimate cited in coverage, as India sales jumped 17.3 percent.
  • Excluding the one-off, profit before tax rose 6.3 percent to Rs 4,428 crore; global specialty sales rose 6.9 percent to $356 million.
  • Shares rose about 4.2 percent to Rs 1,835 as investors focused on underlying growth; US formulation sales fell 8.2 percent to $455 million.

Sun Pharmaceutical Industries reported a 36.2 percent fall in consolidated net profit for the September quarter, as a one-time charge tied to its planned acquisition of Organon weighed on earnings even as revenue grew by double digits.

India's largest drugmaker posted net profit of Rs 1,989 crore in Q2 FY27, down from Rs 3,118 crore a year earlier, after a Rs 1,269 crore exceptional hit linked mostly to Organon-related costs and provisions tied to India's new labour code framework, according to Finimize, citing Reuters. Nation Press, citing the company's regulatory filing, put net profit at Rs 1,988.53 crore and revenue at Rs 16,198.71 crore.

The numbers behind the headline fall

Revenue from operations climbed 11.9 percent year on year to Rs 16,199 crore, from Rs 14,478 crore a year earlier. EBITDA rose 4.8 percent to Rs 4,744 crore from Rs 4,527 crore, though the EBITDA margin contracted to 29.3 percent from 31.3 percent. Excluding exceptional items, profit before tax stood at Rs 4,428.2 crore, up 6.3 percent year on year — the cleaner read on underlying earnings, Nation Press noted.

Research and development spending was Rs 778.4 crore, or 4.8 percent of sales. The proposed Organon acquisition, agreed in April, is valued at about $11.75 billion. Management commentary in related coverage said integration is on track to complete by the last quarter of FY27, with regulatory approval received in multiple markets.

India strength, US pressure

Domestic formulations were the standout. India sales surged 17.3 percent to Rs 5,552.3 crore from Rs 4,735 crore, accounting for 34.5 percent of consolidated revenue. Sun's share of the Indian pharmaceutical market rose to 8.6 percent from 8.3 percent, according to the Pharmarack MAT September 2026 report cited by Nation Press.

The United States moved the other way. US formulation sales fell 8.2 percent to $455 million, contributing about 27 percent of total sales, amid pricing pressure and generic competition. Emerging-market formulation revenue grew 7.6 percent to $350 million, and rest-of-world sales rose 3.1 percent to $241 million.

Specialty sales keep growing

Sun's push into higher-margin specialty medicines continued. Global specialty sales rose 6.9 percent to $356 million, accounting for 21.1 percent of total sales, Finimize reported. That mix matters for the investment case: specialty products are less exposed to the generic pricing pressure weighing on US formulations, and the Organon deal is intended to strengthen the innovative-medicines portfolio further.

How the market reacted, and what to watch

Investors looked past the reported profit fall. Shares gained about 4.2 percent to Rs 1,835, Finimize said; Nation Press reported shares trading 3.99 percent higher at Rs 1,833.30 on the BSE during noon trade on Friday, October 30.

What to watch next is whether India growth holds, whether US sales stabilize, and whether Organon integration closes on the Q4 FY27 timetable without further exceptional charges. For now, the quarter's message is split: a weaker reported bottom line, and a stronger underlying business.
